The proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day moving average surged +5 percentage points on Friday, to 61%, the highest reading since mid-August.

Over the last 3 weeks, this figure has risen +17 percentage points.

This comes despite the S&P 500 remaining roughly unchanged over the same period.

This also ranks among the 3 sharpest improvements in market breadth over the last 3 years.

The market is strengthening beneath the surface.

posts.name: The Kobeissi Letter
posts.text:
The short silver trade is becoming crowded.

Silver's 3-month silver put-call skew is up to -3 points, its highest level since early July.

This metric measures the relative cost of put options to call options and is up +10 points over the last 4 weeks, signaling growing demand for bearish bets on silver prices.

Over the last 12 months, this metric has been higher only 2% of the time.

Meanwhile, speculative investors, including hedge funds and commodity trading advisers (CTAs), sold -$2.2 billion in silver futures over the 3 weeks ending October 13th.

As a result, their net long positioning is down to just +$1.7 billion, the lowest in at least 2 years.

For perspective, this metric stood at +$8.5 billion in December 2025.

Investors are extremely bearish on silver.

JOHN TERNUS SAYS THIS IS THE MOST EXCITING TIME IN HIS CAREER TO BE BUILDING PRODUCTS AT APPLE $AAPL

And he explained why Apple won't even be able to see your personal data

"This is, I'm convinced, the most exciting time in my career to be building product, because AI has so much potential to allow us to change products, make new products."

He said Apple's focus is product, not technology, and if it's done right, nobody has to know AI was involved. "They just want to know that, wow, I was able to do that thing that I couldn't do before, and it was fun and it was easy."

He said Siri will be able to tap into all the personal context on your phone, with privacy built in.

"Nobody else can see it. Apple can't even see it. We don't want to see it, and we can't see it. It is your information."

BREAKING: The average cost of a family’s annual health insurance premium in the US is up +$1,303 YoY, or +5%, to a record $28,303.

This marks the 4th consecutive annual increase of at least +$1,300.

Over this period, the average annual premium for family coverage has surged +$5,884, or +26%.

To put this into perspective, CPI inflation has risen +13% over the same period, or half as much.

Since 1999, the average health insurance premium for a family has soared +$22,494, or +387%.

This represents an average annual growth rate of +6.1%, well above CPI inflation at +2.6% over the same period.

Health insurance has never been more expensive.

President Donald Trump's escalating trade fight with Canada is squeezing the economy north of the border, threatening jobs and adding to families' financial strain as steep U.S. tariffs on roughly $20 billion in goods remain in place.

U.S. tariffs have hammered the country's steel, aluminum, lumber and automobile producers that depend heavily on the American market. Steel exports have fallen by roughly half since the tariffs took effect, while lumber exports were about 20% below 2024 levels earlier this year, according to the Bank of Canada. ALEXANDR WANG SAYS MORE THAN 200 RESEARCHERS AT META $META REPORT DIRECTLY TO HIM

And he says that's exactly the point

"Effectively all the researchers that we hired into this group called TBD, they report directly to me. And it's more of a statement of the fact that this is anti-bureaucracy."

He said the lab still has technical leadership, with pods run by technical leads who tiebreak on technical decisions. But from a people management perspective, "we're just anti-bureaucracy."

"I would be lying if I said I was the best manager to more than 200 people, but part of the point is that they don't need managers. They need a great environment. They are all brilliant. They're all extremely capable. They just need the room to cook."
